summary: Claude invoked hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the task as architectural, ran the full question/design flow, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/ and presented it for approval before any implementation code; after approval it moved to writing-plans.
reasoning: All five acceptance criteria are supported by observed screen text, session-log greps, and files on disk. The escalation to the architectural path with a spec document reviewed before code occurred as the story intended.

observations.description: Codex spec-review gate produced no usable review: agent reported both spec lenses exited 0 but wrote empty {} payloads, verdict-normalize returned 'incomplete', and `status --json` showed no jobs at all (running: [], latestFinished: null). Agent attributed it to the stub companion (codexVersion 0.0.0-stub, no config.toml at $CODEX_HOME). If the stub is meant to return a usable verdict, this is broken fixture/plugin behavior.

During brainstorming the agent announced 'Skipping the Codex approach gate — the three material forks are now settled by your answers, and what's left is mechanical', i.e. it self-skipped a review gate earlier in the flow. Worth confirming this is intended.

The agent added a .gitignore entry for docs/hyperpowers so the spec is deliberately left uncommitted; criterion wording says 'committed spec file', so intent may conflict with the skill's own git instructions.

The in-chat design was presented and approved first, and only then was the spec file written and re-presented — two approval gates in a row for the same design, which felt slightly redundant as a human reviewer.

criteria.evidence: grep of session JSONL: `grep -o 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' *.jsonl | sort | uniq -c` returned `21 hyperpowers:brainstorming`; screen also showed Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) only after the spec was approved.

criteria.criterion: classified ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Assistant text in log: "**Classification: architectural.** The request names a subsystem this repo doesn't have ... So I'll run the full process: questions one at a time, approaches, a sectioned design, then a written spec before any code." File exists: docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-user-preferences-storage-design.md (head shows '# User Preferences Storage — Design ... Status: Approved for planning').

criteria.criterion: spec presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-user-preferences-storage-design.md (not committed). Please review it and let me know if you want any changes before I write out the implementation plan." `git status --short` in workdir at that point showed only `?? .gitignore` — no edits to app.js/index.html.

criteria.criterion: did NOT classify as bounded / skip spec
criteria.evidence: No bounded claim in assistant output; grep of assistant text for 'bounded' returned no classification line, only 'Classification: architectural.' and a committed-to-disk spec file.

criteria.criterion: did NOT classify as spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: Same grep of assistant text showed no spike classification; flow was questions → design → spec doc → writing-plans skill, not a throwaway probe.
